CG-IMPL-010.summary: The COMMON traversal now aims 0.24 through each corner and hands the walker a 0.15 stop radius, instead of aiming 0.6 through it and handing the walker 0.35. The route, C, the ordered eighteen, the arrival predicate, the footprint certification and the dead zone are untouched.
CG-IMPL-010.cause: Two walls meet on the western end of the polyline. FLOOR: the shared walker releases every control inside NAVIGATION_STEER_DEAD_ZONE (0.2) of the point it steers at, so an aim not further past the vertex than 0.2 lets the body park short and vertexReached — which demands an actual crossing at a turn — can never fire. CEILING: the exact-goal handoff only survives while the capsule footprint at the goal is certified by the same planner, which reaches VOXEL_SCALE/2 - PLAYER_CAPSULE_RADIUS = 0.5 from the cell centre; on a cube planet the local up is tilted, so projecting out the normal component of the 1.8-unit gap between an authored foot goal (y 51.05) and a clearance-carrying waypoint (y 52.85) leaves a real tangential residue of 1.8*|up.x|*up.y. At COMMON vertex 6, (-48, ., 18), one cell from the planet-face edge, that residue is ~0.256 by the time the feet are at the vertex plane. 0.2 + 0.256 = 0.456 against a 0.5 reach: the entire slack at that corner is ~0.044 of a unit. The shipped 0.6 spent it several times over, so the handoff was refused and the snapped cell centre stayed the steering target — the CG-IMPL-010 deadlock.
CG-IMPL-010.whyNotTheAuditsOtherOptions: Aiming the overshoot along the OUTGOING leg (the audit’s stated observation) does NOT work: the residue at vertex 6 is on the incoming axis and is present at zero overshoot, and an outgoing-only aim leaves the goal exactly ON the incoming plane, so a body that settles anywhere inside the release radius is still short. Nothing about the terminal vertex required moving C either: with a 0.24 terminal aim, C’s own footprint certifies (its old failing column (-48, ., 10) is never requested).

limits: CPU ONLY. Every terrain, planner, handoff, steering and gait call in the new seam tests is the shipped function over the shipped generator, but no browser, GPU, preview or capture was run and none of this is a hardware pass, a rendering claim or a gameplay acceptance.

The seam tests reconstruct GENERATED terrain: voxelSystem is reset, so live persisted or player-edited voxels are not represented. A column certified here could in principle differ live at (-46, ., 16), (-50, ., 18) or (-48, ., 10). The audit named this same gap.
The seam body is a fixed-step integrator with no momentum. It is conservative (it can only stop earlier than a real coasting body), but it is not the Rapier capsule.

The measured slack at COMMON vertex 6 is about 0.044 of a unit between the release radius and the certified footprint reach. The repair sits inside it with roughly 0.04 on the floor side and 0.06 on the ceiling side, but this corner has NO engineering headroom: any future change to the standing offset, the clearance plane, the dead zone, the capsule radius or the terrain under (-48, ., 18) can reopen CG-IMPL-010. The two new bound tests are written to fail loudly if it does.

Manual/player COMMON traversal remains unmeasured, exactly as producer-arrival-common-findings-review.json records. A movie rail that now walks the corners is not proof that a player can, and this task ran no input, entry or Continue probe.

The CG-IMPL-014 copy assertions compare the resolver output to the signed scene-v3 strings written into the test. They are anchored to real world/flight state (the states are produced by enterShip / enterAtmosphere / notifyLanded / exitShip and read back through commonGroundGuidanceFacts) and to structural relations between the phases, but they do not parse the contract JSON at test time.
Earned Continue, full-story, variants/performance/AV and independent UX review all remain outstanding and mandatory. This report is not any of them.
